EVIDENCE CARD — Harbor-q7m2 index build blocked writes on orders

## Observed environment
Project: /workspace/projects/harbor
Staging deploy, release train 14
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, deploy log header.

## The statement (task text, quoted in full)
db/migrations/0042_add_orders_created_at_idx.sql contains one statement:
  CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at ON orders (created_at);
Source: PRIOR_TASK.md, description.

## Lock observed while the build ran (EXECUTED, captured by the on-call)
pg_locks showed the building backend holding a ShareLock on orders, granted, alongside RowExclusiveLock rows that were not granted.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, psql session capture.

## Waiting writers (EXECUTED)
pg_stat_activity counted 11 backends with wait_event_type Lock running INSERT INTO orders. One sampled waiter had been waiting 00:00:39.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, psql session capture.

## Write stall (EXECUTED)
The checkout service log records the queued write committing after 47 seconds and then draining 11 queued writes in one batch.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, application log.

## Table size (EXECUTED)
reltuples for orders in staging: 18042199.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, psql session capture.

## Reads during the window (EXECUTED)
The dashboard poller logged poll orders ok at 09:41:50, 09:42:10, 09:42:30 and 09:42:50.
Source: PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md, dashboard poller log.

## Limits and unknowns
- Production was not deployed to; only staging is observed here.
- No alternative form of this statement was run, so nothing here establishes what lock any other form would take or how long it would run.
- What happens when an index build fails partway is not shown by the supplied evidence.
- Whether the stall scales with row count is not established: one table at one size was observed.
